source.title: On the training dynamics of deep networks with L2 regularization

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training-accuracy results for networks trained from random initialization, including time to reach training accuracy 1; this bears on V1 using the study's L2 and learning-rate sweeps.
record.gate_note: The paper studies L2 regularization and peak test performance. Its supplementary Figure S1 reports time to training accuracy 1 for FC and WRN setups. Other cited studies' results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Figure S1(b) reports attainment of training accuracy 1 by a randomly initialized convolutional network trained with SGD on CIFAR-10, directly testing V1's training-error outcome.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the paper's subject, but perfect training accuracy is a setup criterion and supplementary observation rather than its principal conclusion. The authors find that time to peak test accuracy scales approximately as 1/(eta lambda) for vanilla SGD, and that sufficiently small nonzero L2 coefficients give similar peak performance when training time is extended accordingly. They propose predicting L2 from a training budget and dynamically scheduling L2; AUTOL2 improves speed and performance without learning-rate schedules but underperforms tuned constant L2 with such schedules. Their infinite-width analysis attributes late deterioration to a decaying kernel.
record.recipe_differences: Studies L2 regularization and its relationship to training time and peak test performance, rather than the claim's general comparison of training-error outcomes across model sizes and recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training-accuracy-1 time varies mildly with L2 and, at sufficiently small learning rates, scales like 1/learning rate. The width-64 CIFAR-10 setup has its peak test accuracy before reaching training accuracy 1.

fits_no_version.finding: The width-2048 fully connected network reaches training accuracy 1 on a small MNIST subset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large fully connected networks can fit a small clean MNIST training set perfectly.

fits_no_version.finding: The width-64 fully connected CIFAR-10 network reaches its test-accuracy peak before perfect training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Best generalization can precede perfect training-set classification.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure S12 varies initialization scale in a residual network and reports early differences that largely disappear at late times.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale can affect early test-accuracy dynamics in WRN while having little effect on late performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure S5 reports learning-rate-dependent test accuracy and subsequent training-loss deterioration with L2, without identifying stability thresholds or curvature trajectories.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: L2 and training duration can reduce learning-rate dependence of peak test accuracy in fully connected networks trained with MSE.

record.code_released: https://github.com/google-research/google-research (JAX is stated; a study-specific code URL is not stated)
record.problems: Training-accuracy times in Figure S1 are only plotted, with no numerical values stated in the text. Experiments use one initialization for learning-rate/L2 comparisons unless otherwise stated. The width-64 case does not establish whether training accuracy later reaches 1.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. Figure S8 reports ImageNet accuracy across learning rates, L2 values, and training budgets, but does not report a training-classification-error result in recoverable text.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100 training error, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and controlled comparisons of smaller convolutional models, early stopping, or recipes leaving substantial training error.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and adding one or two student neurons.
Depth degradation and matched plain-versus-residual comparisons.
Activation-matched initialization in plain networks, signal and gradient propagation, trainable depth, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian initialization.
Learning rates calibrated against initial stability thresholds, accompanying curvature drops, and long-term edge-of-stability dynamics.
Higher-learning-rate tolerance and Fixup comparisons. Figure 3 supplies a paired CNN timing experiment, but the supplied text does not resolve its comparative speed outcome.

missing.what: Training-accuracy trajectories for WRN and CNN without batch normalization across L2 values, including zero regularization. These directly bear on V1 but are omitted; curve heights and endpoints cannot be reliably recovered from the supplied text.

Matched CNN experiments with and without batch normalization report epochs to maximum test accuracy at learning rate 0.01 across L2 values. Extract paired timing and attained-accuracy results before assigning any V6 verdict; the supplied text provides no readable comparative outcome.
missing.locator: Section 2, Figure 3(a,d), with architecture and training details in Supplement A

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Exact figure values were not inferred from detached axis labels. Selecting overparameterized setups limits generality but does not invalidate the directly reported attainment of perfect training accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, smaller-model and early-stopping comparisons are not tested as versioned. The study reports CIFAR-10 and MNIST setups, including a width-64 CIFAR-10 case.
